text.p: Ian Rush with his first goal of the season and Brian Deane scored in the first 10 minutes as Leeds United stunned Chelsea's European aristocrats 2-0 in the English premier league on Sunday.
With their goals, Rush and Deane issued a warning to Ghanaian international striker Tony Yeboah, watching from the substitutes bench, that he faces a battle to regain his place.
Yeboah, having recovered from the knee trouble that has kept him out since March, saw Rush end his 15-match goal drought with his first since joining Leeds from Liverpool in the summer.
It came just two minutes after Deane hit the kind of individualist goal that was worthy of Yeboah at his best.

Chelsea were caught cold and Leeds continued to hustle Ruud Gullit's expensively assembled League of Nations' so that not even Gullit's introduction at the start of the second half could inject the necessary guile into Chelsea's play.

And when Mark Hughes was stretchered off 15 minutes from the end with an ankle injury that required six stitches, Chelsea's misfortune was summed up when replacement Frank Sinclair sent a firm header thudding against the bar.
It was Leeds' third win in four matches and manager George Graham has yet to dip into the cash made available by the club's new owners.
The opener came when Lee Sharpe played a long ball out of defence on the left. Deane drew Frode Grodas off his line and expertly slotted the ball in from the acutest of angles.
Two minutes later Rush's goal famine was over when Dan Petrescu's miskick fell at the veteran Welshman's feet eight yards out to give him the kind of finish that rolled back the years.
Chelsea had their chances but Nigel Martyn kept his third clean sheet in four games with top class goalkeeping.
Rush said later: "Every striker if they don't score lacks confidence but the main thing was to keep battling and I knew it was going to come if I got the chances."
Graham said that with Yeboah and Rod Wallace on the bench, he now had "an embarrassment of riches."
But he said the squad still needs strengthening in other areas.
Gullitt said it was difficult for his side to recover from the bad start.
"We did not create any chances until the second half. But we tried hard for 90 minutes and you cannot ask for more," he said.
